title: _In vivo_ combinatorial knockout screens using CRISPR-Cpf1
protocol: Identify target genes for knockout using Nf2 and Trim72 as illustrative examples.
Design LbCpf1 crRNAs with Benchling or Cas-Designer.
Synthesize oligonucleotides according to the specified schema.
Mix 1 μl of 100 μM forward oligo, 1 μl of 100 μM reverse oligo, and 1 μl of 10x T4 Ligation Buffer.
Add 6.5 μl of ddH2O and 0.5 μl of T4 PNK to the mixture.
Incubate at 37°C for 30 minutes.
Heat at 95°C for 5 minutes.
Ramp down to 25°C at a rate of 5°C per minute.
Reconstitute pRC11, pRG01, or pRC49 with FastDigest Esp3I, FastAP, and 10x FastDigest Buffer to a total volume of 50 μl.
Incubate the reaction at 37°C for 30 minutes.
Run the plasmid digestion on an agarose gel alongside an uncut enzyme control.
Confirm the linearization of the digested plasmid.
Gel purify the linearized plasmid with the QIAquick Gel Extraction Kit.
Dilute the annealed oligos at a 1:200 dilution in ddH2O.
Ligate the diluted annealed oligos into the purified BsmBI-digested plasmid to a total volume of 11 μl.
Incubate the ligation reaction at room temperature for 10 minutes.
Add 1 μl of ligation product to Stbl3 bacteria on ice and mix gently.
Incubate the mixture on ice for 20 minutes.
Heat shock by incubating at 42°C for 45 seconds.
Place bacteria back on ice and incubate for 20 minutes.
Add 250 μl of S.O.C. media to the bacteria, mix well.
Plate the bacterial suspension onto carbenicillin-containing LB agar plates.
The following day, pick colonies from the plates.
Shake overnight in 4 mL of carbenicillin LB broth.
Take 0.5 mL of bacterial cultures and mix with 50% glycerol.
Store the mixture at -20°C for short-term storage or at -80°C for long-term storage.
Purify plasmids from the remaining bacterial cultures using the QIAprep Spin Miniprep kit.
Sequence the plasmids using the primer GAGGGCCTATTTCCCATGAT.
Confirm successful ligation of oligos containing the crRNA array into the expression vector.
Design MCAP library oligos according to the specified schema.
Randomly assign constituent genes to either the first or second crRNA position for each gene pair.
Synthesize the MCAP library using an oligo pool service such as CustomArray.
PCR amplify the library using arrayF_MCAP and arrayR_MCAP primers.
Use a 50 μl reaction volume for PCR amplification.
Incubate at 98°C for 1 minute initially.
Cycle through 32 cycles of 98°C for 1 second, 59°C for 5 seconds, and 72°C for 10 seconds.
Incubate at 72°C for 2 minutes after cycling.
Run the PCR product on a gel.
Purify the gel product with the QIAquick Gel Extraction Kit.
Clone the purified PCR product into the appropriate vector by Gibson assembly using 330 ng of digested vector and 50 ng of PCR-amplified library pool.
Electroporate 1 μl of the Gibson product into Endura ElectroCompetent cells according to manufacturer instructions.
Recover electroporated cells with 975 μl of Recovery Media in a bacterial culture tube.
Shake the cell culture at 37°C for 1.5 hours.
Take 10 μl of the culture and dilute with 990 μl of LB with carbenicillin to create a 1:100 dilution.
Mix 100 μl of the 1:100 dilution further with 900 μl of LB for a 1:1000 dilution.
Plate 100 μl of the 1:1000 dilution on a small carbenicillin LB agar plate to calculate transformation efficiency.
Dilute and plate the remaining cultures on large 245mm LB agar plates using a bacterial spreader.
Count the number of colonies on the small plate the following day.
Multiply the number of colonies by 10,000 to estimate the number of unique colonies in each of the large LB agar plates.
Add 10 mL of LB to the large plates.
Harvest the cells with a cell spreader.
Proceed with plasmid purification using the EndoFree Plasmid Maxi Kit.
PCR amplify the U6 expression cassette using primers MCAP_rdt1_F and MCAP_rdt1_R.
Incubate at 98 °C for 1 min.
Cycle through 15 cycles of \(98 °C for 1s, 60 °C for 5s, 72 °C for 15s).
Incubate at 72 °C for 1 min.
Take 1 μl of the PCR product and amplify with primers MCAP_rdt2_F and MCAP_rdt2_R.
Incubate at 98 °C for 1 min.
Cycle through 20 cycles of \(98 °C for 1s, 60 °C for 5s, 72 ° C for 15s).
Incubate at 72 °C for 1 min.
Sequence the diluted libraries with 5-20% PhiX.
Generate 150bp paired-end reads.
Merge the raw paired-end fastq read files to single fastq files by PEAR with settings -y 8G -j 8 -v 3.
Filter and demultiplex the merged fastq files using Cutadapt, using two different sets of adapters for extraction of crRNA array sequences or the 10mer barcode.
Use cutadapt --discard-untrimmed -g tcttGTGGAAAGGACGAAACACCg followed by cutadapt --discard-untrimmed -a TGTAGATTTTTTT to extract crRNA arrays.
Map the trimmed sequences to the MCAP library using Bowtie: bowtie -v 3 -k 1 -m 1.
Use cutadapt --discard-untrimmed -a AAGCTTGGCGTGGATC followed by cutadapt --discard-untrimmed -g TACTAAGTGTAGATTTTTTT for 10mer degenerate barcodes.
Quantify the resultant sequences to a reference of all possible 10mer sequences.
Tabulate all reads that successfully mapped to both the MCAP library and contained a valid barcode.
Grow HEK293FT cells to 80% confluency in 15-cm tissue culture dishes.
Change media to Opti-MEM one hour prior to transfection.
Transfect HEK293FT cells with 20 ug MCAP lentiviral plasmid library, 10 ug pMD2.G, 15 ug psPAX2, and 1 ug pcDNA3-GFP using polyethyleneimine (PEI).
Change media to DMEM with 10% FBS six hours following transfection.
Collect supernatant at 48 and 72 hours after transfection.
Centrifuge for 10 minutes at 1500g to remove cell debris.
Freeze aliquots in -80°C.
Infect target cells with different lentiviral volumes.
Add 3 μg/mL of puromycin 24 hours following lentiviral infection.
Calculate the ratio of surviving cells after 24 hours compared to initial cell count.
Infect target cells at an MOI of 0.2 for library coverage.
Add 3 μg/mL of puromycin the day after infection.
Continue culturing cells in puromycin-containing media for 7 days.
Expand cell pool in 15 cm tissue culture plates for experiments.
Resuspend cells to a final concentration such that each mouse will receive a 100 μl injection.
Anesthetize the mice according to animal protocol.
Inject 100 μl of a cell suspension containing 4×10^7 cells/ml into the right flanks of nu/nu mice.
Measure tumor sizes by caliper approximately every two days.
Calculate tumor volume using the formula Volume (mm³) = π/6 * x * y * z.
Euthanize mice at 28-35 days after the initial injection for KPD cells.
Harvest primary tumors and lung lobes from euthanized mice.
Freeze harvested tissue in liquid nitrogen, then grind it.
Resuspend each sample in 6 ml of NK Lysis Buffer supplemented with 30 μL of 20 mg/mL Proteinase K in 15 mL conical tubes.
Incubate the resuspended samples at 55 °C overnight.
Add 30 μl of 10 mg/mL RNAse and incubate at 37 °C for 30 min.
Chill the tube on ice, then add 2 ml of pre-chilled 7.5 M ammonium acetate.
Invert and vortex the mixture for 30 seconds, then centrifuge at 4,000g for 10 minutes.
Decant supernatant into a new 15 ml tube, then add 6 ml of 100% isopropanol.
Invert and mix gently 50 times, then centrifuge at 4000g for 10 min.
Discard the supernatant, add 6 ml of 70% ethanol to the pellet.
Mix thoroughly and centrifuge at 4000g for 10 minutes.
Discard the supernatant, remove any residual ethanol by pipette.
Air dry the sample for 20 minutes.
Resuspend DNA by adding 200-500 μl of ddH2O.
Measure concentration by Nanodrop.
Normalize DNA to a concentration of 1000 ng/μl for PCR.
Use 10-20 μg of gDNA per sample for PCR readout from tumor genomic DNA, divided over 5-10 replicate reactions as necessary.
Divide 20 μg of gDNA into 10 replicate reactions for pre-injection cell pool readout.

Perform the first round of PCR using primers MCAP_rdt1_F and MCAP_rdt1_R under thermocycler conditions: 98 °C for 1 min, followed by 15 cycles of \(98 ° C for 1s, 60 ° C for 5s, 72 ° C for 15s), and a final extension at 72 ° C for 1 min.
Pool together the first PCR products from each biological replicate.
Take 2 μl of pooled first PCR products as template for second round PCR using barcoded primers detailed in Table 1.
Perform the second round of PCR under thermocycler conditions: 98 °C for 1 min, followed by 15 cycles of \(98 ° C for 1s, 60 ° C for 5s, 72 ° C for 15s), and a final extension at 72 ° C for 1 min.
Quantify 2 μl of the second PCR products on a 2% E-gel EX using the E-Gel Low Range Quantitative DNA Ladder.
Equally mix the second PCR products of each sample based on their quantities.
Purify the mixed second PCR products using the QIAquick PCR Purification Kit as well as the Gel Extraction Kit.
Sequence diluted libraries with 5-20% PhiX, with 150bp paired-end reads.
Use PEAR to merge paired-end fastq files.
Filter and demultiplex using Cutadapt.
Execute the following command: cutadapt --discard-untrimmed –e 0.1 -a aagcttggcgtGGATCCGATATCa -m 80.
Demultiplex filtered reads with the following settings: cutadapt -g file:fbc.fasta --no-trim, where fbc.fasta contains the 12 possible barcode sequences within the forward primers.
Run this command: cutadapt --discard-untrimmed –e 0.1 -g tcttGTGGAAAGGACGAAACACCg -m 80.
Remove the 5’ DR sequence using: cutadapt --discard-untrimmed -e 0.1 -g TAATTTCTACTAAGTGTAGAT -m 80.
Generate a Bowtie index of the MCAP-MET library using the bowtie-build command in Bowtie 1.1.2.
Map filtered fastq read files to the MCAP-MET reference index using: bowtie -n 2 -k 1 -m 1 --best.
Utilize the same trimmed fastq files as above, but use the barcoded-crRNA plasmid library as the reference Bowtie index for data processing.
Tabulate the number of reads that mapped to each crRNA array within the library using the Bowtie mapping output.
Normalize the number of reads in each sample by converting raw crRNA array counts to reads per million (rpm).
Convert the counts per barcoded-crRNA in each sample to percentages of total reads for analysis at the level of barcoded-crRNAs.
Utilize control crRNA arrays to model the empirical null distribution and identify enriched crRNA arrays that exceed the abundance of the "top" control crRNA array.

Calculate the synergy coefficient (SynCo) for each gene pair using the formula: SynCo = DKONM - SKO¬N- SKOM, where DKONM is the median log2 rpm abundance of all corresponding DKO crRNA arrays and SKO¬N and SKOM are defined as the median log2 rpm abundance of all corresponding SKO crRNA arrays.
Clone specific crRNA arrays using the oligo-cloning protocol described above.
Inject 1.8x10^6 KPD cells per flank into the in vivo tumor model.
Perform tumor growth measurements following established procedures.
Dissect tissues according to previous protocols.
Harvest puromycin-resistant cells seven days after lentiviral infection.
Isolate genomic DNA from harvested cells using the QIAamp DNA Mini Kit.
Design PCR primers to amplify target loci around the cutting site.
Use NCBI Blat to retrieve 600 bp of DNA sequence upstream and downstream of the crRNA cut site.
Copy the ~1200 bp sequence into NCBI Primer-BLAST for primer design.
Select Refseq representative genome for the correct organism under “Primer Pair Specificity Checking Parameters” in NCBI Primer-BLAST.
Perform PCR on the isolated genomic DNA using primers designed in step 3.
Run PCR amplicons on a 2% E-gel EX.
Purify known band size PCR products using QIAquick Gel Extraction Kit.
Denature and anneal 200 ng of purified PCR product in NEB Buffer 2 according to the manufacturer's protocol.
Digest annealed PCR product with T7E1 at 37°C for 45 minutes.
Load digested PCR products into a 2% E-gel EX.
Quantify DNA fragment abundance using E-Gel™ Low Range Quantitative DNA Ladder (ThermoFisher).
Calculate the mutation frequency using the formula: 100 x \(1 – \(1- fraction cleaved)<sup>1/2</sup>).
Dilute PCR amplicons and prepare sequencing libraries using the Nextera XT kit.
Sequence diluted PCR amplicons using paired-end reads on an Illumina sequencer.
Map paired reads to the reference genome (expected sequences provided in FASTA form) using BWA-MEM with the command: bwa mem -t 8 -w 200.
Run VarScan v2 using the pileup2indel command, which utilizes Samtools mpileup.
Filter indels to those occurring within a ±7 bp window around the predicted cut site.
Sum the variant frequencies of filtered indels to determine the indel frequency.
